title: rusolve.result/1
description: The result envelope `rusolve mip --format json` writes as the one JSON object on stdout. Written by crates/rusolve-cli/src/envelope.rs. Solver logs never appear on stdout in this mode: with output_flag=true they go to stderr. Numbers: JSON has no inf/nan, so a non-finite solver value (a dual bound of -inf before the first incumbent, a gap of inf with no incumbent, an unlimited time_limit) is null. An agent that must distinguish 'no incumbent' from 'unbounded bound' reads has_solution together with dual_bound.

schema_version.description: The version tag of this envelope. Breaking changes bump it and ship a new schema file.

git.description: The commit the binary was built from: `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD`, with `-dirty` appended when tracked files had uncommitted changes (captured by crates/rusolve-cli/build.rs). Omitted when the build had no git (a source tarball).

profile.description: The option profile in force, from RUSOLVE_PROFILE: `recommended` (the default) or `highs-1.15.1` (HiGHS 1.15.1 semantics, every rusolve-specific option off). Set the same variable to rerun.

engine.description: Which solver stack ran the model. 'highs-port' is crates/rusolve-ekk, the faithful HiGHS translation (RUSOLVE_MIP_HIGHS=1 for `mip`, the default for `solve`). 'native' is the rusolve-mip / rusolve-lp stack (the default for `mip`, --legacy-lp / --ipm for `solve`). 'clarabel' is the interior-point conic route for continuous SOCP and convex QCQP models (crates/rusolve-cli/src/conic_solve.rs); it adds the `conic` object. Both others print the same envelope; `run.options` is empty on the native stack, which has no HiGHS option registry.

input.description: The model as read, before presolve.

edits_applied.description: Only from the MCP server: the number of `modify` edits applied to the model handle since it was loaded. When present and positive, `path` names the handle (`<model_id> (edited)`) and `sha256` is the SHA-256 of a canonical dump of the edited model, not of a file.

sha256.description: SHA-256, lower-case hex, of the model file's bytes exactly as read from disk: for a `.gz` model these are the compressed bytes, so `shasum -a 256 <file>` reproduces it.

rows.description: HighsLp::num_row_: constraint rows. The MPS objective (N) row is not one of them.

integer_cols.description: Columns with HighsVarType::kInteger in HighsLp::integrality_. 0 for a pure LP, including a model whose integrality_ vector is empty.

status.description: Closed enum, one value per HighsModelStatus (the full mapping, with reasons, is the doc comment of envelope::result_status). HiGHS's kSolutionLimit is set by mip_max_nodes, mip_max_leaves, mip_max_improving_sols and mip_max_stall_nodes: it is reported as 'NodeLimit' when the node count reached mip_max_nodes and as 'SolutionLimit' otherwise. 'Error' also covers the case where Highs::run returned HighsStatus::kError. The five HiGHS error statuses share 'Error'; the limit-like and exceptional ones keep their own name so an agent never has to guess between a stopped solve and a broken one.

objective.description: The objective of the reported solution, including the model offset (HighsInfo::objective_function_value). null when there is no solution or the value is not finite.

dual_bound.description: HighsInfo::mip_dual_bound, in the minimisation sense HiGHS reports it in, whatever the model's objective sense. null when infinite, which with has_solution false means no incumbent had been found yet.

gap.description: HighsInfo::mip_gap, the relative gap HiGHS computes in HighsMipSolverData::limitsToGap. A fraction, not a percentage: 0.01 is 1%. null when infinite (no incumbent).

qp.description: Convex QP: present only when the model has a quadratic objective (a Hessian). The check that ran before the engine: the QPLIB-style class code (objective, variables, constraints; Furini et al. 2019), the convexity verdict, how it was reached, the diagonal shift added for a Q that was indefinite by rounding only, and the engine that solved it.

shift.description: Added to the diagonal of Q (subtracted for a maximisation) before solving; 0 when none.

min_eigenvalue_estimate.description: Smallest eigenvalue of Q (of -Q for a maximisation) when a failed test produced an estimate; null otherwise.

hessian_nonzeros.description: Nonzeros of the symmetrised Q, both triangles.

engine.description: The engine that produced the answer.

engine_selection.description: default: HiPO first, QUASS when HiPO does not end Optimal. user: the solver option was named and is honoured as given.

fallback.description: true when HiPO did not end Optimal and QUASS produced the answer.

fallback_from_status.description: The status HiPO ended with when fallback is true; null otherwise.

class.description: The problem class the router assigned, the same name `rusolve classify --format json` reports. For a plain LP or MIP, which the router does not read, it is `mip` when the model has integer columns and `lp` otherwise (`rusolve solve` on a MIP solves the relaxation and says `lp`).

engine.description: The engine that solved the class: `highs-port` or `native` for LP and MIP (as solver.engine), `hipo` or `quass` for a convex QP (the same name as `qp.engine`; the selection and any fallback are in the `qp` object), `clarabel` for conic and convex QCQP, `gc-linearization` for general constraints (linearized, then the HiGHS port). solver.engine stays the stack that ran.

convexity.description: `convex` for a solved quadratic class (convex QP, conic); absent for a linear class. A nonconvex model is refused (rusolve.error/1), never solved.

diagnostics.description: Present only when there is one: lint warnings found before the solve (RS2001 weak big-M, RS2002 coefficient range, RS2003 huge or free column; off with --no-warnings), the infeasible set of rows (RS2010) or primal ray (RS2011) of an Infeasible or Unbounded result, and a violated row of the returned solution (RS2012). Each item is a rusolve.diagnostics/1 diagnostic (docs/schema/rusolve-diagnostics-1.schema.json); codes are explained by `rusolve --explain`.

limit.description: Present when a limit or an interrupt ended the solve (status TimeLimit, NodeLimit, SolutionLimit, IterationLimit, MemoryLimit, ObjectiveBound, ObjectiveTarget or Interrupted). The incumbent, bound and gap are the top-level objective, dual_bound and gap.

enforced_by.description: solver: HiGHS checked the limit itself. watchdog_interrupt: the wall-clock watchdog (--watchdog) requested the interrupt callback and the solve ended at its next limit check; status is TimeLimit. watchdog_kill: the solve did not react within the grace period (--watchdog-grace), so the watchdog reported the last state the callbacks saw (no solution, nodes and LP iterations as of the last callback) and ended the process with exit code 0.

improving.description: Whether the incumbent was still improving. Tracked only with --log-format jsonl or --watchdog (they register the improving-solution callback); otherwise tracked is false and the other fields are null.

last_improvement_s.description: Seconds from the solve start to the last improving solution; null when none.

still_improving.description: A reporting convenience: an incumbent exists and the last improvement came within the last tenth of the run.

has_solution.description: HighsSolution::value_valid: an incumbent primal solution exists and solution.columns describes it.

lp_iterations.description: HighsInfo::simplex_iteration_count: the total LP iterations over the tree, the number the CSV line reports in field 5.

time_s.description: Wall-clock seconds of read + solve + report. Not reproducible across runs; everything else in this envelope is reproducible at threads=1.

work.description: Deterministic work of the MIP solve in simplex synthetic ticks. The same model, options and seed give the same value on every run and machine at threads=1. 0 when the model took no MIP path.

phases.description: Per-phase statistics of the MIP solve (rusolve-ekk mip/mip_stats.rs). Every *_s field is wall time and varies between runs; everything else is reproducible at threads=1. Absent when the model took no MIP path.

status.description: HighsPresolveStatus of the last MIP presolve.

rows_after.description: Of the presolved model the search ran on (the last one after restarts).

reductions.description: Entries of the postsolve stack by reduction type (FixedCol, RedundantRow, DoubletonEquation, ...). Bound tightenings and coefficient changes leave no entry.

lp_iterations.description: HighsMipSolverData::firstrootlpiters: LP iterations of the first root LP solve.

lp_objective.description: HighsMipSolverData::firstlpsolobj; null when no root LP was solved.

node_time_s.description: Wall seconds in the root node: root LP, root separation and root heuristics (the port has no separate clock for them).

rounds.description: HighsSeparation::separationRound calls (root and tree) of the top-level MIP.

pool_cuts.description: Cuts in the global cut pool at the end.

cuts_found.description: HighsSeparator::numCutsFound: cuts the separator put in the pool.

improving_incumbents_by_source.description: Incumbents that improved the upper bound, by HighsMipSolverData::solutionSourceToString. Heuristic calls are not counted by the port.

time_s.description: Wall seconds after the root node returned; 0 when the solve ended earlier.

by_source.description: LP simplex iterations and LP solves by what asked for the solve (root, root/tree separation, strong branching, node re-solves by origin and depth, each heuristic family, untagged), sub-MIPs included. Reporting only; sources with no solve are omitted.

work.description: The parts of stats.work: work = simplex_ticks + unit_ticks * (propagation_units + feasibility_jump_units + presolve_units).

simplex_ticks.description: HiGHS simplex synthetic ticks (INVERT build + per-iteration FTRAN/BTRAN/update).

propagation_units.description: Column nonzeros walked by HighsDomain activity updates (propagation, probing).

feasibility_jump_units.description: FeasibilityJump totalEffort (nonzeros touched), HiGHS's own effort count for that heuristic.

presolve_units.description: Row nonzeros walked by HPresolve::getRowPositions, the presolve loops' row traversal.

unit_ticks.description: Ticks per propagation, presolve or FeasibilityJump unit.

first_incumbent.description: Wall time and work when the first incumbent was found; null if none.

propagation_events.description: Reporting-only tallies of objective propagation and reduced-cost fixing in the MIP solve, sub-MIPs included: runs, bound changes (domain-change stack growth) and cutoffs; and of conflict analysis by source (conf_*_tree/heur/inflp/boundlp/degen: calls, explained, conflicts added to the pool, literals added). They never feed work or the search.

wasm.description: Present only when a Wasm hook component was loaded for this run (`rusolve mip --wasm-hook`, MCP solve `wasm_hook`; crates/rusolve-wasm, docs/design/wasm-hooks.md). The component name (its file stem) and the call counters: every call is exactly one of ok, declined (valid 'no opinion'), traps, out_of_fuel or invalid (out-of-range/NaN), plus total fuel consumed. A component can only reorder the search, never change the answer.

component.description: The component name: the file stem of the loaded .wasm/.wat file.

ok.description: Calls whose answer the solver used.

declined.description: Valid 'no opinion' answers (branch_score nonzero, cut_score NaN, select_node -1, or the records not fitting the memory cap).

invalid.description: Wrong-shape answers (NaN score, out-of-range node index).

fuel_used.description: Total interpreter fuel consumed over all calls.

run.description: How the solve was asked for, so it can be asked for again.

threads.description: The threads option in force. The port MIP path pins threads=1 for reproducibility; --threads is not accepted there.

time_limit.description: Seconds, null when unlimited (the HiGHS default).

node_limit.description: mip_max_nodes, null when --node-limit was not given.

options.description: The --opt key=value settings as given, values as strings. A repeated key keeps the last value, which is what the solver kept. Options left at their profile default are not echoed here.

general_constraints.description: Present when the model has general constraints (indicator, SOS, piecewise-linear, min/max/abs/and/or, semi-continuous): what was linearized (added_columns, added_rows, objects by kind, the route per object), and whether the answer was checked against the user's objects (verified, violations).

conic.description: Present only when solver.engine is 'clarabel' (a model with quadratic constraints or cones). clarabel_status is Clarabel's own status; reduced_accuracy is true for its Almost* statuses. For a solution: objective_primal / objective_dual (model sense, offset included), checker (the `rusolve check` verdict on the user's rows and cones at the stated tolerance), row_duals (d objective / d rhs of each constraint row, in the model's sense, by name) and cone_duals (the dual vector of each user cone). For Infeasible or Unbounded: certificate, the Farkas vector or the unbounded ray, with `verified` set by checking it on the conic form; a certificate that does not verify turns the status into Unknown.

solution.description: The incumbent, in original-model space after postsolve. Present only when --solution or --include-solution was given, so the default envelope stays small on a model with thousands of columns.

columns.description: One entry per column of the model as read, in column order. Names are the model's own; a model that came in without a name for some column gets HiGHS's minimal generated name (c0, c1, ...). Empty when has_solution is false.

start.description: Present only with --start <file> (read side; crates/rusolve-cli/src/warm.rs). The MIP start, matched to the model by column name and passed through the ported Highs::setSolution. A complete start is checked first and an infeasible one is an input error (exit 3), so a start that appears here was accepted.

complete.description: True when the start names every column; a partial start is completed by the solver.

objective.description: Objective of a complete start (model sense, offset included); null for a partial one.

became_incumbent.description: True when the feasible complete start was installed as the first incumbent (HighsMipSolverData::checkAddSolution); null for a partial start.

final_incumbent_is_start.description: True when the final incumbent equals the start (1e-9); null for a partial start.

improved_on_start.description: True when the final objective is strictly better than the start's; null for a partial start.

added_rows.description: Present only with --add-rows <file>. Rows added to the model before the solve; each passed the validity gate (malformed rows always rejected; rows that cut off the mip_debug_solution_file solution rejected when it is set). input.rows counts the added rows; input.sha256 is the model file's.

debug_solution_gate.description: True when mip_debug_solution_file was set, so the gate could prove a row invalid.

basis.description: Present only with --basis <file> (read side): a HiGHS basis file read as readBasisStream does.

installed.description: False for a model with integer columns: the port's MIP solve does not use a basis.
